lessons.title: Mediation and dispute resolution
lessons.description: Learn language for mediation and alternative dispute resolution.

vocabulary.example: The parties agreed to try mediation.
The mediator met with both parties.
The mediator helps facilitate discussion.
Each party reviewed the proposal.
They hope to resolve the dispute.

sections.heading: Professional dialogue
sections.body:
A: Would your client consider mediation?
B: We are open to discussing the proposal.
A: The mediator can help the parties explore options.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Use neutral phrases such as “explore options” and “seek a resolution” to avoid implying that a party has already accepted an offer.

quiz.question: Who facilitates mediation?
quiz.explanation: A mediator facilitates discussion between parties.

quiz.question: What does resolve a dispute mean?
options: Find a way to settle it
quiz.explanation: To resolve a dispute is to settle or solve it.

lessons.title: Legal research and citations
lessons.description: Read and discuss legal sources, authorities and citations in English.

vocabulary.example: The judgment cites a relevant authority.
The provision sets out the filing period.
The statute governs the procedure.
Please verify the citation.
The lawyer discussed a relevant precedent.

sections.heading: Research note
sections.body: The memorandum identifies the statutory provision, explains its wording and cites the authority relied upon.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Distinguish the source from the argument: “The statute provides…” reports a text; “This suggests…” introduces an interpretation.

quiz.question: What is a statutory provision?
options: A section or rule in legislation
quiz.explanation: A provision is a part of a law that sets out a rule.

quiz.question: What should you do with a legal citation?
quiz.explanation: Legal citations should be checked against the actual source.

lessons.title: Written submissions and legal arguments
lessons.description: Structure a concise written submission with issues, reasons and requested relief.
objectives: Connect facts to a legal argument

vocabulary.example: Counsel filed written submissions.
The appeal raises one ground.
The argument relies on the wording of the statute.
Accordingly, the applicant requests relief.
The prayer for relief appears at the end.

sections.heading: Model paragraph
sections.body: For the reasons set out above, the applicant submits that the decision should be reconsidered. Accordingly, the applicant respectfully requests the relief stated below.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: A clear submission identifies the issue, gives reasons supported by sources, then states the requested order. Local court rules determine required form and terminology.

quiz.question: What is a ground of appeal?
options: A reason relied on to challenge a decision
quiz.explanation: A ground states a reason why a decision is challenged.

quiz.question: Which phrase introduces a conclusion?
quiz.explanation: Accordingly signals a conclusion or result.

lessons.title: Client communication and legal costs
lessons.description: Explain fees, disbursements and next steps to a client in clear language.

vocabulary.example: The lawyer explained the fee.
The filing fee is a disbursement.
This is an estimate of the likely costs.
The office sent an invoice.
The engagement letter defines the scope of work.

sections.heading: Client email example
sections.body: Dear Client, our current estimate covers the work described in the engagement letter. Court fees and other disbursements may be charged separately. We will contact you before any material change to the scope of work.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Avoid promising a fixed total unless the engagement terms support it. Explain assumptions, exclusions and the next update in plain language.

quiz.question: A disbursement is usually…
options: An expense paid on behalf of the client
quiz.explanation: A disbursement is an expense paid for a client, such as a filing fee.

quiz.question: What defines the scope of work?
options: The work agreed with the client
quiz.explanation: The scope of work describes the legal services covered by the engagement.
